1.title: Interested in IT
1.description: I was in 9th grade when I first got interested in IT. I started doing internships at local companies to get a feel for the industry and insights into the different roles and responsibilities.

2.title: Tech. Highschool
2.description: I enrolled in a tech-focused school to get more understanding and got in touch with programming and a lot more of different technologies. I also enrolled to get permission to study at a highschool.

3.title: Side projects
3.description: I started working on side projects to apply what I learned and to explore my interests further. I built a few projects, including a Discord bot and just small Python scripts to get a better understanding of programming.

4.title: Herrenknecht AG
4.description: I applied at Herrenknecht AG as a Dual Student in the field of IT. I got accepted and started working there in July 2025.

5.title: Dual Student at Herrenknecht AG
5.description: Alongside working at Herrenknecht AG, I was enrolled as a dual student at DHBW Karlsruhe, splitting my time between practical work and theoretical coursework.

6.title: Changing direction
6.description: I left the dual-study program at DHBW Karlsruhe - splitting time between lectures and full-time work wasn't the right fit, so I looked for a path that's more hands-on.

7.title: Ausbildung: Fachinformatiker Anwendungsentwicklung
7.description: Since 1 September 2026, I've swapped the split dual-study model for a full apprenticeship (Ausbildung) as a Fachinformatiker für Anwendungsentwicklung at Herrenknecht AG - full-time and fully hands-on through 2028.

projects.title: What I'm building and where each project stands.

1.title: Portfolio Platform
1.description: Personal portfolio with component architecture, motion, responsive layout, and section-based storytelling.
1.about: This site - built to actually learn Next.js properly instead of just reading about it, and to have something online that's mine instead of a template. Everything runs on a BMW M / racing theme, down to the small stuff.
highlights: Hand-built BMW M livery theme and motion carried through every page, not just the homepage
Traced the real Nürburgring Nordschleife track geometry for the /experience timeline map
A couple of hidden easter eggs, including a launch-control sequence and a small race mini-game

2.title: Pygame
2.description: Creating something like Mario to learn the library and refresh my python skills. It will be open sourced once it's in a presentable state.

3.title: Discord Bot
3.description: My own Discord bot for running a server: ticket system, audit log, welcome messages, moderation tools and a few minigames.
3.about: One of my first projects, recently rebuilt from scratch. Every feature is its own cog that gets loaded automatically, so adding something new is just dropping a file into a folder.
highlights: Ticket panel with claim/close buttons - closed tickets get archived as a .txt transcript
Audit log for joins, leaves, deleted and edited messages, with a word-level diff for edits
Per-server settings via /config that survive restarts
Minigames like rock-paper-scissors, number guessing and a typing speed test that catches copy-paste

4.title: Lunair
4.description: An invite-only photo feed for me and my friends to share pictures, thoughts and little stories from everyday life.
4.about: Started as a blog idea and turned into a small private social feed instead. There's no public sign-up - you only get in with an invite link, so it stays between friends. Posts can be a few photos or just text, and everything lands in one shared feed.
highlights: Invite-only login, with a profile picture, banner and a grid of your own posts on your profile
Posts with multiple photos or text only, all in one shared feed
Up to 3 reactions per post using your own custom stickers
Comments with replies and reactions on comments too
Photo carousel you can flip through on desktop, plus a fullscreen view with zoom
A shared pet called Luni that everyone feeds and pets together - with a streak that keeps going as long as someone looks after it each day

5.title: Karteikarten App
5.description: A flashcard app for creating and studying digital flashcards. Built as a project during my studies at DHBW.
5.about: A flashcard app for creating and studying your own cards - built as the practical project during my studies at DHBW, with a real Postgres/Drizzle backend behind it instead of just local state.
highlights: Card overview to create, edit, and delete your own flashcard sets
Self-study mode with a flip-card animation, progress saved per card
Login/register so cards and progress follow you across devices

6.title: LUNAS OS
6.description: My personal HUD-style home dashboard for everyday life and vocational school: todos, appointments, timetable, grades, notes from Obsidian - and an animated Live2D character in the middle.
6.about: Built for myself first, with my vocational school (Berufsschule) as the main use case. The start page is a one-pager: a Live2D character in the center, with the day's data orbiting around it as satellites. Everything school-related hangs off its Lernfeld. Single user, GitHub login only - which is also why the repo is private.
highlights: One-pager with a Live2D character that follows your cursor, surrounded by the day's data - countdown to the next exam, timetable, 14-day timeline
Greeting and a daily brief read aloud via the Web Speech API, plus adding todos by dictation
Notes pulled straight from my Obsidian vault, including wiki links, images and callouts
Achievements as a graph styled like Obsidian's graph view, drawn on canvas with d3-force
Weather for Offenburg, private file storage and per-subject pages with files, todos, appointments and a grade average

7.title: lunagraph
7.description: A code knowledge graph for Next.js/TypeScript projects, so Claude Code can look a project up instead of searching through it from scratch every time.
7.about: A learning project. lunagraph indexes a project once into a SQLite file - who imports what, and later who calls what and which route touches which table. The end goal is an MCP server that lets Claude Code query all of it. LUNAS OS is the test project.
highlights: Phase 1 is done: files and imports get indexed, including the @/ alias and barrel files
Against LUNAS OS: 52 files and 228 import edges in under half a second, zero unresolved imports
Up next: symbols and calls, Next.js routes and Drizzle tables, then the MCP server

8.title: lunaracing
8.description: A telemetry tracker for Le Mans Ultimate: record laps, store them and compare them afterwards - sector times, braking points, where I'm leaving time on the table.
8.about: Up next. A small ingest service reads the live telemetry from LMU's shared memory, writes every lap to Postgres, and a Next.js frontend shows lap comparisons. It brings my sim racing hobby together with what I do at work: backend, data modelling and lots of writes.

privacy.title: Data protection
privacy.intro: Most of this site does not use analytics, tracking, or cookies, and does not collect any personal data. The Pit Wall guestbook is the exception - here is what it collects and why:
privacy.messagesText: Anything you post to the Pit Wall (your display name and message, plus your Discord name and avatar if you sign in) is stored and shown publicly on that page.
privacy.discordBefore: Signing in with Discord is handled by Discord's own OAuth login - this site receives your Discord user ID, display name, and avatar URL, which are stored so your entry can show up as a Discord post. See
privacy.discordAfter: for how Discord itself handles your data.
privacy.spamBefore: Submitting to the Pit Wall runs a Cloudflare Turnstile check, which processes some technical signals about your browser/request to tell humans from bots - see
privacy.spamAfter: . A salted, one-way hash of your IP address is also stored for up to 24 hours to rate-limit repeated submissions; the hash cannot be reversed back into an IP address, and it is not linked to your message.
privacy.removal: Want a guestbook entry removed? Get in touch using the contact details above.
